rulings.conclusion: Choose up to two eligible creatures together before either enters. All chosen cards become held, then enter one at a time. Finish the entire Gate spell before resolving entry triggers.
rulings.notes: 409.1f explicitly names Heaven’s Gate; 101.4a/d delay triggers. Do not choose the second creature from a Wellkius draw. Zero/one/two is allowed.

rulings.conclusion: Sheva chooses zero, one or two creatures from mana with creature-side summed cost <=7 together. Hold both before entering one at a time. Any pending card is excluded from mana count; an entry EXlife or static change can alter later entry replacement checks.
rulings.notes: 409.1c/f; 810.3a. Costs evaluated at selection; later entry restrictions/replacement effects evaluated for each entry.

rulings.conclusion: Variety5 requires five distinct costs among your battlefield elements. Twinpact creatures contribute their creature-face cost only, never their spell-face cost. Shield-zone G castles are excluded by default element scope.
rulings.notes: Official QA directly establishes battlefield Twinpact face scope; applying it to Sheva is inference. 403.1 scopes unqualified element references to battlefield.

rulings.conclusion: When Variety5 is active, ordinary nondestruction movement (bounce, mana, shield, deck) fails even for your own effects. A forbidden move never reaches EXlife replacement, so it does not consume its shield. Destruction is permitted and may be replaced by EXlife/escape.
rulings.notes: QA46947 directly establishes Sheva prevents mana movement even when that movement is a replacement. Prohibition priority101.2; no direct named Sheva+EXlife QA located. Deep-zone send explicitly bypasses protection: QA47945.

rulings.conclusion: Ninja Strike end-of-turn deck return is nondestruction and thus stays while Variety5 applies. Revolution Change and Ninja Change swaps fail when outgoing creature cannot leave; incoming card does not enter.
rulings.notes: QA examples directly establish swap failure when the outgoing creature cannot leave, including EXlife keeping its shield intact on a failed swap. Sheva/Ninja-specific conclusion is inference; see701.26.

rulings.conclusion: Only a summoned entry triggers Mika’s top-four ability. Gate/Wellkius/Sheva entries are not summons. Choose any number (including zero) of revealed creatures; no cost cap. Remaining cards go to mana.
rulings.notes: Saiphogate latest official flavor text explicitly warns its cheat entry does not trigger Mika.

rulings.conclusion: Mika selects/holds all creatures to enter before the first enters; enter them one by one, then move remaining revealed cards to mana, then resolve queued entry abilities. Revealed cards remain in the deck until moved/held. EXlife can consume a still-deck revealed card; do not duplicate/move an already-shielded card later.
rulings.notes: 409.1c/f;101.4d;400.2b. Revealing alone is not a zone move. Named Mika+EXlife-revealed-card QA not located, so final interaction is rules-based inference.

rulings.conclusion: Deck reaching zero loses immediately, including during an effect. Held cards do not count toward deck count. Do not postpone loss to after remaining revealed cards return/go to mana or the next draw.
rulings.notes: 104.2b,409.1c. If revealing alone does not move cards, revealing the whole deck alone does not empty it. Selecting/holding all remaining cards does empty it.

rulings.conclusion: At own turn start, Mika’s ability triggers. Check >=4 own cost8+ battlefield creatures at resolution, not a locked turn-start snapshot. If count drops below4 before resolution, do not win; if another start effect raises it to4 before resolution, win. Mika itself need not remain after its ability has triggered.
rulings.notes: 603.4 expressly says conditional triggered abilities check resolution and need not satisfy at trigger time.110.3b holds triggered effects;41567 confirms turn-player effects win before opponent Shako start-draw.

rulings.conclusion: Wellkius draws one mandatorily, then may put one blocker creature from hand. Any civilization and evolution blockers are permitted, with legal evolution base required.
rulings.notes: This is broader than Gate, Achernar and Saiphogate, which require Light non-evolution.

rulings.conclusion: Blocker must exist on the hand card at selection. A battlefield-only granted blocker does not make cards in hand eligible. However do not restrict eligibility to literal printed keyword only: abilities which function in all zones can give blocker in hand, e.g. Survivor after official 2023 change.
rulings.notes: 110.4; official change directly allows Azole-alpha as Gate target through Survivor in every zone.

rulings.conclusion: Win-battle trigger observes a completed battle win, not necessarily opponent destruction. Equal powers cause both to lose and no win. Slayer destruction occurs after battle-result triggers resolve, so a winning creature may die later yet Wellkius already triggered. An observer whose ability was ignored immediately before battle loser left does not trigger.
rulings.notes: 115.3b/d;701.13b-d; QA44586 directly confirms pre-departure observer state. Once triggered, later removing Wellkius does not cancel its effect.

rulings.conclusion: When both escape and EXlife are available on destruction, choose which replacement to apply. If escape is declined, mandatory EXlife applies. Escape can select any own shield including an EXlife shield; no S-trigger use.

Oshioki Moon triggers on each own shield card departure while Hades remains in the battlefield, including EXlife replacement and escape. If Hades leaves simultaneously with shield departure, it does NOT trigger. A G castle departing the shield zone should trigger too by card text, as should each card in a multi-card shield.
rulings.notes: 46566/46567 directly resolve simultaneous Hades removal. G-castle/multi-card-shield applicability follows unqualified “card left own shield zone”; no named direct QA located.

rulings.conclusion: Rudolf triggers only when attack is declared targeting its controller or Rudolf itself, never when blocking redirects another attack to Rudolf. Resolve the triggered random discard before deciding blockers.
rulings.notes: Track declared target UID, not post-block or post-redirection defender.

rulings.conclusion: First attacked per turn is history across the whole turn, including attacks on the player before Rudolf arrived. Entering after a prior player attack does not reset first. Each Rudolf needs its own qualifying predicate: controller already attacked OR that specific creature UID attacked. An attack at a different creature does not consume it.
rulings.notes: Carne analogue QA44382 directly establishes “first this turn” events before arrival still count; applying that history rule to Rudolf is inference. No direct Rudolf prior-arrival QA located.

rulings.conclusion: Gio may reveal any number of OTHER cost9 cards in hand; it cannot reveal itself. In hand, a Twinpact with either card face cost9 qualifies, once per physical card. Reveal choice occurs during cost determination before mana payment; preserve optional choices and show revealed information to opponent.
rulings.notes: Card directly says other and optional. QA44609 directly establishes both hand costs.601.1e determines payable cost before601.1f payment.

rulings.conclusion: Apply existing cost increases/reductions to Gio with the chosen reveal reduction; preserve minimum1, and each physical revealed card counts once. Its self-reduction works in executing zone; do not treat revealing as a later queued enter trigger or arbitrary automatic full-hand reveal.
rulings.notes: 110.4e;601.1e/f. Exact ordering with all supported reducers depends their printed minimum/conditional wording. No special Gio stacking QA located.

rulings.conclusion: Takeback may choose any battlefield element cost<=3, own or opponent, creature or noncreature. Move it tapped to OWNER’s mana, not necessarily opponent mana. Default “element” does not select a G castle in shield zone or an evolution-under-card.
rulings.notes: 403.1 element zone;109.2c element structure. If a replacement sends it somewhere other than mana, it never enters mana and no mana tapped placement occurs.

rulings.conclusion: Genmu ignoring cost<=5 spell effects includes Takeback’s charger effect; then it resolves no spell effects and finishes in grave unless an independent external replacement/finish destination applies. Charger is not an unconditional finish-to-mana override.
rulings.notes: Charger is self-movement replacement;609.8a self replacement normally precedes external replacements. If ignored, no such replacement remains. Official Genmu page verified2026-10-22; no direct named Genmu+charger QA located.

rulings.conclusion: Charger takes priority over external after-cast grave-to-deck-bottom replacements. Takeback finishes to mana even when cast by a source which says put it at deck bottom instead of grave, unless the charger effect itself is ignored (e.g. Genmu). This is self-movement replacement priority609.8a; do not chain a second replacement onto charger mana placement.
rulings.notes: QA32907 DandarudaBB+Spellbook Charger and QA_old38040 Wozreck+charger directly say mana, not bottom. A later separate instruction can only move that spell if it tracks/references its new zone correctly; QA_old34922 says a grave-only instruction cannot find a charger in mana.

unresolved: No direct named official QA located for Sheva+EXlife/Ninja, Mika revealed leftovers consumed by EXlife, Rudolf attacks before arrival, or Gio stacking; these are explicitly classified as inference.
